title: The Next Game: A Systematic Literature Review of Career Self-Management and Well-Being in Elite Athletic Career Transitions
abstract: This study contributes to career transition research by examining complex career transitions through the case of elite athletes. Transitions out of sport are complex, involving multiple boundary crossings, high novelty, and negative affect. They are often triggered by abrupt endings, such as injury, and accompanied by significant resource loss. Using the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this systematic review synthesizes findings from 41 studies on how elite athletes navigate the transition to post-sport careers. We examine the relationship between career self-management (CSM) and well-being before and after the transition, alongside the role of personal and contextual factors. Findings show that early CSM, including self-exploration, skill development, and transfer, buffers resource loss and supports well-being. Social support, athletic identity, and transition characteristics are associated with well-being and sustained CSM-engagement. While the CSM–well-being relationship may be reciprocal, most evidence comes from cross-sectional designs, underscoring the need for longitudinal studies to clarify causal dynamics.
